fields.title: Evaluation conjointe des besoins en matière d’Education et Protection RDC-2026
fields.body:
Le rapport de l’évaluation conjointe des besoins d’Education et de Protection menée en collaboration avec le secteur de la Protection met en évidence les résultats suivants :

- Taux d’abandon de 12,5 % au cours de l’année scolaire 2025-2026, principalement lié aux difficultés socio-économiques des ménages, aux déplacements forcés, aux travaux domestiques, ainsi qu’aux mariages et grossesses précoces.
- 131 établissements sur 266 (50 %) rapportent des absences scolaires liées à la gestion des menstruations.
- 76 responsables d’établissements sur 266 (28%) affirment que les établissements ont subi des pillages ou vols perpétrés par des groupes armés depuis le début de l’année 2026, tandis que 47 sur 266 (18%) ont relevé l’occupation de salles de classe par des forces ou groupes armés.
- L’inclusion des enfants en situation de handicap demeure limitée, avec peu de mesures spécifiques favorisant leur participation et leur maintien à l’école.
- Seuls 51 établissements sur 266 (19 %) disposent d’un accès à l’eau potable provenant de leur principale source d’approvisionnement.
- 114 établissements (43 %) ne disposent pas de latrines séparées pour les filles et les garçons.
- 101 établissements sur 266 (38 %) signalent la présence d’enfants présentant des signes de détresse psychosociale, notamment des cauchemars, une tristesse persistante, une anxiété élevée, de la fatigue extrême, des comportements violents ou de l’isolement.
- Seuls 70 établissements sur 266 (26%) disposent d’un mécanisme de référencement VBG adapté aux enfants et permettant l’orientation vers des services spécialisés.

Malgré ces défis, les consultations avec les enfants montrent que l’école reste perçue comme un espace de protection, de stabilité et d’espoir. Comme l’a souligné un enfant de 8 à 11 ans : « **A l’école, on étudie et on oublie la guerre**. »

fields.title: Central African Republic: Situation Report No. 94, as of 17 November 2026
fields.body:
**HIGHLIGHTS**

- Despite a still volatile context, some humanitarian movements have resumed around Zémio.
- Infrastructure has been installed in Ouham-Pendé to help prevent agro-pastoral conflicts and reduce tensions between herders and farmers.
- 3,900 students received school kits in Kaga-Bandoro and M’brès.

**GENERAL CONTEXT**

Haut-Mbomou Prefecture – South-East

The security situation remains volatile in the Zémio area, despite a relative improvement recently observed along certain roads around the town. In this context, humanitarian actors have gradually resumed some movements and activities in areas affected by movement restrictions that have been in place since September. A limited resumption of civilian movement has also been observed on the main road corridors, while staff from peripheral health facilities have been able to travel to Zémio to replenish medical supplies. No incidents have recently been reported on these routes. A humanitarian organization also conducted movements along the Zémio-Dembia axis to carry out assessments. Given the continuing volatility of the security environment, humanitarian partners are closely monitoring developments and maintaining existing security and risk-management measures.

 **HUMANITARIAN NEEDS AND RESPONSE**

 **Health**

Haute-Kotto Prefecture – Central

On 11 November, the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and its partner International Medical Corps (IMC) concluded their campaign providing comprehensive care for women living with obstetric fistula. A total of 33 patients received specialized treatment in Bria, with an 88 per cent success rate. 15 other patients faced transportation challenges in reaching Bria from Ndele in Bamingui-Bangoran Prefecture. To improve access to services in that area, a second two-week campaign is being conducted in Ndele from 12 to 26 November 2026.

**Multi-sector**

Vakaga Prefecture – North-East

On 11 November, the NGO COHEB, under a labour-intensive work project implemented through the Emergency Project to Support the Stabilization and Recovery of Refugees and Host Communities in the Lake Chad Basin (PASRRC), distributed cash assistance to 400 beneficiaries, including 150 Sudanese refugees and 250 members of host communities. Through the cash-for-work approach, each beneficiary received 30,000 CFA francs to support livelihoods and meet priority household needs.

fields.title: République centrafricaine : Rapport de situation N° 94 au 17 novembre 2026
fields.body:
**FAITS SAILLANTS**

- Malgré un contexte toujours volatil, certains mouvements humanitaires ont repris autour de Zémio.
- Des infrastructures pour prévenir les conflits agro-pastoraux et réduire les tensions entre éleveurs et agriculteurs dans l’Ouham-Pendé.
- 3 900 élèves reçoivent des kits scolaires à Kaga-Bandoro et M’brès.

**CONTEXTE GÉNÉRAL**

Préfecture du Haut-Mbomou – Sud-Est

La situation sécuritaire demeure volatile dans la région de Zémio, malgré une accalmie relative observée récemment sur certains axes routiers autour de la ville. Dans ce contexte, les acteurs humanitaires ont progressivement repris certains déplacements et activités dans les zones affectées par les restrictions de mouvement en vigueur depuis septembre dernier. Une reprise limitée de la circulation des populations civiles a également été observée sur les principaux axes concernés, tandis que le personnel des formations sanitaires périphériques a pu se rendre à Zémio pour s’approvisionner en médicaments. Aucun incident n’a été rapporté récemment sur ces itinéraires. Une organisation humanitaire a par ailleurs effectué des déplacements sur l’axe Zémio-Dembia afin de conduire des évaluations. Compte tenu de la volatilité persistante du contexte sécuritaire, les partenaires humanitaires continuent de suivre étroitement l’évolution de la situation et maintiennent les mesures de gestion des risques et de sécurité en vigueur.

**BESOINS ET RÉPONSE HUMANITAIRE**

**Santé**

Préfecture de la Haute-Kotto – Centre

Le 11 novembre 2026, le Fonds des Nations Unies pour la population (UNFPA) et son partenaire International Medical Corps (IMC) ont clôturé leur campagne de prise en charge holistique des femmes vivant avec une fistule obstétricale. Au total, 33 patientes ont bénéficié de soins spécialisés à Bria, avec un taux de réussite de 88 %. 15 autres patientes ont été confrontées à des difficultés de déplacement pour atteindre Bria depuis Ndele dans la préfecture du Bamingui-Bangoran. Afin d’améliorer l’accès à ces services dans cette préfecture, une seconde campagne de deux semaines a lieu à Ndele du 12 au 26 novembre 2026.

**Multisectoriel**

Préfecture de la Vakaga – Nord-Est

Le 11 novembre 2026, l’ONG COHEB, dans le cadre du projet de Travaux de haute intensité à main d’œuvre (THIMO) mis en œuvre à travers le Programme d’appui d’urgence à la stabilisation et au relèvement des réfugiés et des communautés hôtes dans le bassin du Lac Tchad (PASRRC), a procédé à une distribution monétaire au profit de 400 bénéficiaires, dont 150 réfugiés soudanais et 250 membres des communautés hôtes. A travers l’approche « travail contre rémunération », chaque bénéficiaire a reçu une assistance en espèces de 30 000 FCFA, visant à soutenir les moyens d’existence et à répondre aux besoins prioritaires des ménages vulnérables.

fields.title: The Bundibugyo Ebola Outbreak in Africa: Six-Month Situation and Response Report
fields.body:
## **Executive summary**

This report examines the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak and the continental response from the declaration on 15 May 2026 to the evidence available for preparation of the six-month milestone on 15 November. It integrates pathogen and transmission knowledge, zoonotic origin and One Health, epidemiology, clinical care, operational performance, country experiences, research, financing, logistics, essential health services, social consequences and preparedness.

The principal finding is that substantial response capacity was mobilized, but persistent transmission and mortality indicate that this capacity did not consistently translate into sufficiently early detection, timely access to care, complete identification of transmission networks and reliable local service delivery in DRC. The introduction that began the outbreak also remains unexplained, so the risk of further spillover in the affected landscape persists independently of progress against human-to-human transmission.

### **Key findings that should guide the next phase**

**1. The burden remains overwhelmingly concentrated in the DRC.** Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria provide distinct experiences of managing cross-border or travel-associated infection. Their outcomes should be assessed against their own case histories and observation periods. France’s imported case and medical evacuations to other countries belong in a separate international account so that the same patient is not counted twice.

**2. Early growth was exceptional, but historical comparison requires matched definitions.** The early reported burden substantially exceeded burden observed during the comparable early periods of major 2014 and 2018 Ebola epidemics, although direct quantitative comparison is constrained by differences in case categories included, uncertainties in disease onset and official detection and declaration, ascertainment and observation intervals. Historical comparisons should therefore preserve the original case classifications and reporting periods.

**3. Contact tracing misses most new cases:** Only 11% of confirmed cases (1,146 of 10,659 with onset from week 19 to week 45) came from the contact lists, against a target of 95%. The response found the other 89% outside those lists, which means many transmission links were identified too late to list and monitor the contacts. The daily contact follow-up \[text continues beyond the visible page\].

### **Five headline numbers in the analytical snapshot**

By 8 November 2026, five countries had reported 11,021 confirmed cases and 5,358 deaths, a crude case-fatality ratio (CFR) of 48.6%.

The DRC carries almost all of this burden, with 10,990 cases and 5,354 deaths (CFR 48.7%). Uganda reported 20 cases and 2 deaths, Kenya 9 and 2, Nigeria 1 imported case and no deaths, and France 1 imported case and no deaths.

In the DRC, 67 health zones in eight provinces have reported at least one confirmed case, and 51 of 67 health zones reported a case in the last 21 days.

National notifications have held at about 460 to 480 confirmed cases a week since late September; the epidemic is a sustained plateau and not yet declining.

fields.title: Operational Update - Central African Republic - July - September 2026
fields.body: UNHCR's operations in the Central African Republic (CAR) are built on protection through presence, the cornerstone of the humanitarian response. Amid volatile security conditions and the spillover of the crisis in Sudan, UNHCR also remains ready to respond to emergencies. Durable solutions are another top priority supporting the voluntary, safe, and dignified return of Central African refugees, their sustainable reintegration, and their contribution to national development. Together with the Government of CAR and its partners, UNHCR provides protection and multisectoral assistance to internally displaced people (IDPs) and refugees, including Sudanese and Chadian refugees, while promoting durable solutions for Central Africans returning home. Its work is aligned with national priorities: the National Development Plan, the National Strategy for Durable Solutions and the Solutions Support Platform established under the 2022 Yaoundé Declaration.

fields.title: République Centrafricaine (RCA) Mise à jour opérationnelle Trimestrielle | Juillet - Septembre 2026
fields.body:
Les opérations du HCR en République centrafricaine (RCA) reposent sur la protection par la présence, pilier central de la réponse humanitaire. Dans un contexte marqué par la volatilité sécuritaire et les répercussions de la crise soudanaise, le HCR reste également mobilisé pour répondre aux urgences.

La recherche de solutions durables constitue une autre priorité majeure, notamment l’appui au retour volontaire, sûr et digne des réfugiés centrafricains, ainsi qu’à leur réintégration durable et à leur contribution au développement national.

Aux côtés du Gouvernement centrafricain et de ses partenaires, le HCR assure la protection et une assistance multisectorielle aux personnes déplacées internes (PDI) et aux réfugiés, notamment soudanais et tchadiens, tout en promouvant des solutions durables pour les Centrafricains de retour. Les interventions s’alignent sur les priorités nationales : le Plan national de développement, la Stratégie nationale pour les solutions durables et la Plateforme d’appui aux solutions issue de la Déclaration de Yaoundé de 2022.

fields.title: Chad : Humanitarian Situation in Lac Situation Report N° 02 (30 October 2026)
fields.body:
*This report was produced by OCHA in collaboration with the authorities and humanitarian partners. It primarily covers the period from 1 to 30 October 2026 and incorporates findings from the July 2026 mid-term evaluation of the response to internally displaced persons (IDPs). The next report will be published at the end of November 2026.*

**KEY POINTS**

- 307,206 displaced people in the province according to IOM Round 26, including 268,064 IDPs, 17,100 returnees, and 22,042 former IDPs who have returned.
- More than 75,000 IDPs have been hosted across 16 sites in the Fouli and Kaya departments since May 2026. New population movements continue to be reported and remain under verification.
- An encouraging improvement in the cholera situation was observed between 13 and 26 October, followed by a resurgence of 12 new cases in Kiskawa. However, the case fatality rate remains high (5.78%), well above the WHO emergency threshold, requiring the need to strengthen prevention, surveillance, and WASH interventions.
- The areas of Liwa, Kiskawa, Kadoulou, and Daboua are among those most exposed to security risks. This insecurity directly contributes to population displacement, loss of livelihoods, and reduced access to basic services.
- Four incidents were reported in the departments of Fouli and Kaya, affecting several civilians and resulting in dozens of deaths as well as abductions, a toll that would have been even higher without the intervention of the defense and security forces.
- Despite the scale of needs, the protection sector remains the least covered, with only 0.3% of targeted people assisted.
- A concerning deterioration in livelihoods has been observed linked to low rainfall.
- US$10.6 million has been mobilized through humanitarian emergency funding mechanisms, including CERF, the Regional Humanitarian Fund, and anticipatory action, to support the response.
- Significant humanitarian needs remain unmet due to insufficient funding, particularly in protection, shelter and site management, education, health and nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), and food security.
- The revitalization of the Grand Cadre Nexus and the review of convergence zones offer an opportunity to strengthen integrated investments by linking emergency response, access to essential services, social cohesion, and resilience.

fields.body:
*En octobre 2026, la situation de protection au Nord-Kivu est restée critique, marquée par une intensification des affrontements dans les territoires de Masisi, Walikale et Rutshuru. Cette situation se serait traduite par l’usage d’armes lourdes et de frappes de drone, des représailles contre les civils ainsi que des déplacements forcés.*

**FAITS SAILLANTS DE LA PÉRIODE**

**Intensification des hostilités** : Des affrontements auraient opposé un groupe armé à une coalition de groupes armés dans les territoires de Masisi et de Walikale, et des frappes de drone auraient visé Binza (Rutshuru).

**Déplacements forcés** : Près de 2 580 ménages (environ 12 900 personnes) auraient été déplacés, dont 546 à Busanza (Rutshuru) et 450 à Kasake (Masisi).

**Engins explosifs** : Des projectiles tombés sur Kasake auraient fait 4 morts et 6 blessés, et des engins explosifs largués sur Kangati auraient tué 2 garçons.

**Représailles et riposte Ebola** : Des enlèvements contre rançon accompagnés de meurtres et des attaques de structures sanitaires à Butembo et Beni auraient été commis.

fields.title: Anticipatory Action Plan (AAP) for Riverine Floods – Southwest Region Cameroon
fields.body:
*This plan by WHH Anticipatory Humanitarian Action Facility (WAHAFA) partners Christian Blind Mission (CBM) and the Presbyterian Church in Cameroon (PCC) shows how Anticipatory Action supports flood-prone communities in Limbe, Fako Division, Cameroon, to act before severe riverine flooding occurs.*

This locally developed Anticipatory Action Plan (AAP) combines rainfall forecasts and community observations to trigger early actions addressing health risks, property damage, displacement and food insecurity. Developed with communities, local authorities and organizations of persons with disabilities, the AAP includes drainage clearance, early warning communication and the distribution of water purification tablets, hygiene supplies, mosquito nets and food items.

Using a two-phase trigger mechanism based on forecasts from the National Observatory on Climate Change (ONACC) and local observations of soil saturation, the AAP enables the activation of anticipatory actions with a lead time of approximately 3-9 days and the release of pre-agreed finance from the WAHAFA Fuel funding.

fields.title: Cameroon: North-West and South-West Situation Report No.87, July to September 2026
fields.body:
**HIGHLIGHTS**

- More than 1,600 protection incidents recorded in the North-West and South-West regions.
- Nearly 900 people displaced in the North-West and South-West regions due to violence and insecurity.
- More than 4,000 people affected by floods and landslides, with about 500 displaced and five deaths reported.
- Four improvised explosive devices incidents recorded in the North-West region.
- A total of 736 children with severe acute malnutrition received life-saving treatment in partner-supported treatment centres.

**SITUATION OVERVIEW / HUMANITARIAN ACCESS**

During the reporting period July-September 2026, the humanitarian situation in Cameroon’s North-West and South-West (NWSW) regions remained fragile and deteriorated further amid continued clashes between State security forces (SSF) and non-State armed groups (NSAGs). Persistent insecurity, including kidnapping for ransom, arbitrary arrests, the proliferation of illegal checkpoints, extortion, and roadblocks, continued to restrict population movements, hinder access to basic services and livelihoods, and heighten protection risks for affected communities.

The situation remained volatile, with at least 11 improvised explosive devices (IED) incidents recorded during the reporting period, including 10 in the North-West and one in the South-West. While these attacks primarily targeted SSFs and their convoys, civilians remained at significant risk of injury or death from accidental explosions.

Attacks and threats against education intensified ahead of the 2026/2027 school year. NSAGs enforced school-related restrictions, imposed school levies in some areas, and increased intimidation of education personnel, including the abduction of five teachers in Wum (Menchum division, North-West). In September, armed actors also attacked a secondary school in the North-West, disrupting learning activities.

Humanitarian needs remained severe across the two regions, exacerbated by successive lockdowns imposed by NSAGs between 1 and 21 September. The measures restricted movement, disrupted education, livelihoods, and economic activities and limited access to essential services. Lockdown enforcement through threats and sporadic attacks resulted in civilian casualties in both regions and further affected already vulnerable communities.

Continued clashes between parties to the crisis triggered new population displacement and humanitarian needs across the North-West and South-West. In Momo division, an estimated 875 people (175 households) were displaced from Diku to Tikom during the reporting period with many families seeking refuge in nearby bushes. Heavy rainfall that caused flooding and landslides on 5 August affected over 4,157 people, displaced more than 500, caused five reported deaths, including a pregnant woman, and destroyed or damaged 16 houses infrastructure, livestock, and community water systems in Limbe (Fako division), Kumba (Meme division) in the South-West, and in Tinifoimbi Village (Boyo division) in the North-West. While many affected households have returned, those whose shelters were destroyed or damaged remain displaced and in need of assistance. Priority needs include shelter, food assistance, health, WASH, protection, education and livelihood support. In coordination with OCHA and area-based coordination co-chairs, humanitarian partners delivered multipurpose cash assistance, shelter support, psychosocial services, and gender-based violence prevention interventions across affected communities, in addition to the assistance delivered by authorities.

Humanitarian access remained constrained due to insecurity, prolonged lockdown and the presence of illegal checkpoints along key road corridors, including the Bamenda-Widikum axis in Momo division and the Bamenda-Ndop road. These restrictions significantly hindered population movements and limited the transportation of agricultural produce. The operational environment remained highly challenging and required continuous access negotiations amid a fragile, volatile, and rapidly evolving context.

fields.title: DR Congo: Ebola response cannot succeed without broader humanitarian effort | NRC
fields.body:
A more comprehensive and inclusive approach is essential if the spread of Ebola is to be halted, warns the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)

Press release

[DR Congo](https://reliefweb.int/themes?categoryId=47) Published 19. Nov 2026

Six months after Ebola was declared in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo), the outbreak remains out of control and continues to devastate communities.

Insecurity remains a major concern in affected areas, where regular violent attacks continue to cause displacement, hindering access to healthcare and disrupting contact tracing and the monitoring of Ebola patients. Violent conflict allows the virus to spread unchecked, with devastating implications for the population. Experience on the ground demonstrates that containing the virus requires more than just a health response. It also requires a broader humanitarian approach that puts community protection and recovery at the heart of its priorities.

Against this backdrop, maintaining access to essential services and strengthening infection prevention and control (IPC) are critical. In more than 100 schools, 25 health centres, and 10 communities, the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) supports the installation of triage systems and handwashing facilities, the provision of hygiene supplies, and the adoption of good IPC practices. These interventions help create safer environments for children, teachers, patients and health workers, while strengthening institutional capacities to prevent and mitigate the risk of Ebola transmission.

At the community level, risk awareness and communication activities bring key messages closer to the population. Working directly with local communities is central to addressing concerns and misconceptions, encouraging protective behaviours, strengthening trust and allowing for the rapid uptake of recommended prevention measures.

“I am living proof that early action saves lives,” explained one Ebola survivor in Ituri during an interview with NRC staff.

“As soon as I recognised the symptoms, I sought medical assistance. This decision saved my life and helped protect my family, my colleagues and the wider community. We really need to make sure people understand how important it is to act early. Without community awareness, we cannot fight this virus effectively,” he added.

The impact of the outbreak also extends beyond the immediate risk of infection. The high levels of disruption and fear triggered by the outbreak can affect children's emotional well-being and ability to learn. Through its Better Learning Programme (BLP), NRC works with schools to help children manage stress and anxiety, maintain their concentration and continue engaging in learning despite the challenges they face.

“Responding effectively to Ebola goes beyond preventing the transmission of the virus. It is also about protecting children, safeguarding the future of entire populations, and supporting those who survive Ebola to safely reintegrate into their communities,” said Silvia Beccacece, NRC emergency response team leader in Ituri.

“Every day, our teams work alongside communities, engaging with people, listening to their concerns and mobilising them to play an active role in the response. Six months into this outbreak, sustaining these efforts is a shared responsibility, and our commitment must remain strong for as long as people need support,” she added.

As the outbreak evolves, it is essential that the response becomes more effective and more embedded in communities. Authorities, humanitarian organisations and donors all have a role to play in ensuring that community-based prevention and protection activities can continue. This requires sustained political attention, meaningful support for local engagement, and predictable funding. Maintaining these efforts is essential not only to contain the outbreak, but also to protect the lives, rights and dignity of the people and communities affected.

**Notes to Editors:**

- The latest figures on confirmed cases and deaths are available here: [DRC Ebola Bundibugyo - Epidemic Intelligence Dashboard](https://inrb-umie.github.io/BDBV2026-Epidemic_Dashboard/)
- Among the 68 health zones affected by the outbreak, NRC operates in 19, contributing to infection prevention and control and protection efforts. NRC's interventions combine support to health facilities, schools, and communities, to strengthen hygiene, reduce exposure to the virus and promote safer practices.
- The Africa CDC has repeated its view that the current outbreak remains out of control ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/africa-cdc-says-ebola-outbreak-still-out-control-six-months-since-it-was-2026-11-15/?taid=6afacf73718669000140b8ed&utm_campaign=trueAnthem:+Trending+Content&utm_medium=trueAnthem&utm_source=twitter))
- The World Health Organisation has warned that insecurity remains one of the greatest obstacles to the current response ([WHO)](https://www.afro.who.int/countries/democratic-republic-of-congo/news/six-months-accessing-hard-reach-communities-key-halting-ebola-outbreak)

**For more information or to arrange an interview, please contact:**

fields.title: Central African Republic BVD Readiness - DREF Operational Update (MDRCF034), 18 November 2026
fields.body:
**Description of the Event**

**Date of event**

17-05-2026

**What happened, where and when?**

Between 15 and 18 May 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared an outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) caused by the Bundibugyo strain as a major public health emergency. This declaration was rapidly echoed by the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC).

At that time, the outbreak mainly affected three provinces in the DRC, namely Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu. As of 18 June 2026, a total of 33 health zones had reported confirmed cases, distributed as follows:

21 out of 36 health zones (58.3%) in Ituri;  
 11 out of 34 health zones (32.4%) in North Kivu;  
 1 health zone in South Kivu.

These figures confirmed that Ituri Province remained the epicentre of the outbreak.

According to WHO data available on 18 June 2026, the DRC had recorded 896 confirmed EVD cases, including 208 deaths and 78 recoveries. Cross-border transmission had also been reported in Uganda, with 19 confirmed cases, including two deaths and seven recoveries.

Although the Central African Republic (CAR) had not reported any confirmed EVD cases at that time, the country remained at high risk of disease importation due to its proximity to the affected areas of the DRC. This outbreak, the seventeenth recorded in the DRC and the second associated with the Bundibugyo strain, had progressively expanded towards provinces located near the CAR border, notably Haut-Uélé. Available epidemiological information indicated a high likelihood of ongoing undetected transmission in this province, which serves as an important population movement corridor towards the border provinces of Bas-Uélé and South Ubangi.

Furthermore, several public health alerts had been reported in areas close to the CAR border, including:

The report of a death associated with a suspected viral haemorrhagic fever in Libenge Health Zone, South Ubangi Province, which hosts Central African refugees;  
 A report dated 18 June 2026 from the Chief Medical Officer of Yakoma Health Zone regarding a suspected EVD case in a locality bordering Ouango-Gambo Health District in CAR.

In this context, the combination of proximity to areas of probable transmission, intense cross-border population movements, repeated epidemiological alerts, and limited preparedness capacities fully justified the activation of a DREF preparedness operation. The operation aimed to anticipate and reduce the risk of EVD introduction and spread in CAR through proactive preparedness, community-based surveillance, and community engagement activities.

However, the epidemiological situation evolved in a concerning manner, with the outbreak progressively spreading to provinces that share a direct border with CAR. In August 2026, Bas-Uélé Province, which borders CAR, reported its first confirmed EVD case in Buta Health Zone, becoming the sixth affected province in the DRC. The confirmed case was linked to travel from Haut-Uélé Province, highlighting the persistent risk associated with population movements between affected areas and border districts in CAR.

As of 19 August 2026, the DRC had reported 5,208 confirmed cases and 2,476 deaths, compared to 896 cases and 208 deaths on 18 June 2026. In addition, 84 per cent of identified contacts were under follow-up. On the same date, another confirmed EVD case was reported in Viadana Health Zone, Bas-Uélé Province, in close proximity to the Haut-Mbomou, Mbomou, and Basse-Kotto health districts of the Central African Republic.

The progression of the outbreak is particularly alarming. While three provinces and 33 health zones were affected as of 18 June 2026, the situation had expanded to six provinces and 55 affected health zones by 19 August 2026. This continued geographical expansion brought the outbreak significantly closer to the CAR border and substantially increased the risk of virus introduction into the country.

Since the launch of the preparedness operation, sixty-four (64) suspected EVD cases have been reported and investigated in CAR. All laboratory test results returned negative for Ebola Virus Disease.

By the end of October 2026, the regional situation had deteriorated further. Most DRC provinces bordering CAR were affected by EVD, including Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé, South Ubangi, and North Ubangi. Geographical proximity, combined with the strong historical and family ties between communities living along the Ubangi River, facilitates significant formal and informal cross-border population movements.

As of 25 October 2026, the epidemiological situation in the DRC reported:

10,060 cumulative cases;  
 4,887 deaths;  
 2,684 recoveries;  
 1,008 patients admitted to treatment centres;  
 a case fatality rate of 48.6%;  
 a contact tracing rate of 81.6%.

These cases were distributed across eight provinces and 66 health zones or health districts.

At the same time, the Central African Republic has progressively strengthened its preparedness capacity. The national preparedness level increased from 42 per cent at the beginning of the operation to 68 per cent during the latest assessment conducted at the end of August 2026. The 30-day acceleration plan validated in early October 2026 aims to raise this level to 95 per cent.

As part of this acceleration plan, the Incident Management System has been decentralized to bring coordination closer to the highest-risk regions and their border health districts. Efforts are underway to make Ebola Treatment Centres fully operational in Obo, Bangassou, the Bimbo University Teaching Hospital, and PK24. Surveillance at points of entry has been reinforced, as have risk communication and community engagement activities, under the leadership of the Minister of Health.

The Central African Red Cross (CRCA), which leads the Safe and Dignified Burials pillar, has trained fifteen teams of ten volunteers each to ensure adequate coverage of high-risk localities.

Finally, on 22 and 23 October 2026, CAR and the DRC met in Bangui for a cross-border coordination meeting aimed at strengthening information sharing, exchanging experiences, and improving joint preparedness measures to prevent and control any potential spread of the outbreak in health districts on both sides of the border.

fields.title: Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak: Democratic Republic of the Congo | Kenya | Nigeria Weekly External Situation Report 27, Data as of 15 November 2026
fields.body:
**Event description**

The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues at a high and sustained level of transmission. During epidemiological week 46 (9 – 15 November 2026), 442 confirmed cases and 239 confirmed deaths were reported, compared with 458 cases and 228 deaths in week 45; the national seven-day average has remained between 62 and 65 cases per day, and a new health zone, Watsa in Haut-Uélé, reported its first confirmed cases. Over three epidemiological weeks (weeks 44 – 46 compared with weeks 41 – 43), reported cases decreased by 6.7% and deaths by 4.6%, with a decline in Ituri partly offset by continued intense transmission in Nord-Kivu, where Beni remains the health zone with the most cases, and by rising incidence in Mangala, Mambasa and Mutwanga. Deaths in treatment centres increased in week 46 and the proportion of deaths occurring in the community fell to 59% (142 of 239), its lowest weekly level since August. In Kenya, the last patient was discharged on 11 November, and all contacts have completed their follow-up; the 42-day countdown is under way, and the event has not yet been declared over. In Nigeria, all 62 contacts completed their 21-day follow-up on 13 November and no secondary case was identified; surveillance continues in both countries. Additionally, Nigeria started the 42 days countdown on 27 Oct after the case was medically evacuated to Switzerland on the 26 October 2026.

In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, insecurity in Beni, Mabalako and Bafwasende, strikes over unpaid salaries in several provinces and community resistance to safe burials continue to constrain surveillance and response operations.

fields.title: Réunion conjointe :Cluster Nutrition et Pronanut: Compte rendu de la réunion mensuelle du mois d'octobre 2026
fields.body:
La réunion conjointe PRONANUT-Cluster Nutrition du 27 octobre 2026 a réuni environ 60 partenaires. Les échanges ont porté sur la méthodologie de calcul des personnes dans le besoin pour le HNRP 2027, la préparation de la revue annuelle 2026 du PRONANUT, la réponse nutritionnelle à Ebola dans les CTE/CT et les interventions des partenaires.

Les discussions ont mis en évidence un faible niveau de rapportage et des besoins nutritionnels encore non couverts. Elles ont souligné la nécessité de renforcer la coordination, d’actualiser les projets dans Activity Info (HPC 2026) et de concentrer les interventions sur les zones prioritaires insuffisamment couvertes.

fields.title: Cluster Protection RDC : Aperçu du monitoring de protection au Sud-Kivu - Faits saillants et tendances majeures du mois de octobre 2026
fields.body:
*En octobre 2026, la situation de protection au Sud-Kivu s’est considérablement détériorée, marquée par une intensification des affrontements entre groupes armés dans les territoires de Walungu, Kabare, Kalehe, Mwenga et Fizi. Cette dégradation se serait traduite par la présence d’engins explosifs dans des zones d’habitation, des actes de représailles, ainsi que des recrutements forcés, y compris d’enfants.*

**Forte hausse des violations** **des droits** : 2 466 violations ont été identifiées en octobre, soit +62% par rapport à septembre (1 524), le niveau le plus élevé depuis juin.

**Engins explosifs** : Des engins explosifs auraient été lancés lors des affrontements à Kaziba, dans le territoire de Walungu, causant la mort de plusieurs civils, dont une femme et ses deux enfants, ainsi que la destruction d’une école.

**Recrutement d’enfants** : 44 allégations de recrutement et d’utilisation d’enfants ont été documentées, notamment à Kalehe, Mwenga, Fizi et dans la plaine de la Ruzizi.

**Représailles** : Des civils accusés de collaboration auraient été arrêtés, torturés et auraient vu leurs maisons incendiées, notamment à Itombwe (Mwenga) et à Kabare.

fields.title: HCR Tchad | Rapport opérationnel hebdomadaire du 15 novembre 2026
fields.body:
Réponse d’urgence à l’Est

L’afflux continu de réfugiés soudanais en quête de sécurité au Tchad accentue la pression sur les capacités d’accueil, particulièrement à Tiné, où le centre de transit accueille désormais plus de 9 000 réfugiés, soit neuf fois sa capacité initiale. Entre le 1er et le 15 novembre 2026, 5 411 nouveaux réfugiés soudanais ont été enregistrés dans les provinces du Ouaddaï, du Wadi Fira et de l’Ennedi Est, portant à plus de 989, 827 le nombre total de nouveaux arrivants accueillis au Tchad depuis le début du conflit au Soudan en avril 2023. Ces nouvelles arrivées sont principalement liées à la persistance des violences et de l’insécurité au Darfour, ainsi qu’aux attaques contre les infrastructures civiles. Conformément à sa tradition d’asile et au principe de non-refoulement, le Gouvernement tchadien a continué de garantir l’accès au territoire aux personnes fuyant le conflit au Soudan et à la protection internationale. Le HCR et ses partenaires ont poursuivi les activités d’enregistrement, de suivi de protection, de relocalisation et d’assistance vitale, avec une attention particulière portée aux personnes les plus vulnérables. Bien que le rythme des arrivées reste inférieur aux pics précédemment observés, notamment en septembre, la poursuite des mouvements transfrontaliers continue d’exercer une pression importante sur les capacités d’accueil, les services de protection et, plus largement, la réponse humanitaire dans l’est du Tchad. La relocalisation des réfugiés soudanais vers des sites plus sûrs se poursuit. Entre le 1er et le 15 novembre, le HCR et la CNARR ont relocalisé 2 170 réfugiés soudanais depuis la zone frontalière d’Adré vers Metché, dans le Ouaddaï, leur permettant ainsi d’accéder à de meilleures conditions de protection et aux services essentiels. Au 15 novembre 2026, 154 370 réfugiés restaient en attente de relocalisation dans les zones frontalières, notamment à Adré et à Tiné. La poursuite des opérations de relocalisation demeure essentielle pour réduire la pression sur des capacités d’accueil fortement sollicitées, offrir aux réfugiés des conditions plus sûres et améliorer leur accès à la protection et à l’assistance humanitaire. Mise en œuvre progressive de l’Approche basée sur la vulnérabilité et les capacités dans les sites de réfugiés de l’Est du Tchad. Entre le 26 et le 31 octobre 2026, le HCR et ses partenaires ont poursuivi la mise en œuvre de l’Approche basée sur la vulnérabilité et les capacités (ABVC) dans les sites accueillant des réfugiés dans l’est du Tchad. Au total, 48 025 ménages réfugiés à Aboutengué, Metché, Zabout, Djabal, Goz-Amir et Kerfi ont reçu les résultats de leur évaluation. Ces résultats permettront au HCR et à ses partenaires de mieux cibler et prioriser l’assistance en fonction des vulnérabilités et capacités identifiées, tout en renforçant le suivi des ménages ayant des besoins spécifiques. La communication des résultats et le mécanisme de gestion des réclamations se sont poursuivis à Metché, Milé et Touloum, tandis que les préparatifs ont été finalisés à Amdjarass en vue du déploiement de l’ABVC à Ouré Cassoni à partir du 3 novembre. Entre le 2 et le 8 novembre, le HCR et ses partenaires ont facilité le départ de 21 réfugiés soudanais de l’est du Tchad vers le Canada. Douze réfugiés ont bénéficié d’un programme de la réinstallation, deux d’une reunification familiale et sept personnes reinstallés au Canada par les voies complémentaires. Le HCR poursuit ses efforts en faveur des solutions durables dans l’est du Tchad, notamment à travers l’accompagnement des réfugiés et le traitement des dossiers de réinstallation et de regroupement familial.

fields.title: Vakaga: Authorities and Residents Welcome the Renewal of MINUSCA’s Mandate
fields.body:
17 November 2026

**In Vakaga Prefecture, in the northeastern Central African Republic, local authorities and residents welcomed the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate, which was adopted on November 12, 2026, by the United Nations Security Council. In this region, which faces persistent security and humanitarian challenges—particularly in areas bordering Sudan and Chad—the Mission’s presence is seen as a key factor in protecting civilians, ensuring stability, and fostering socioeconomic development.**

**By Mamouda Tankoano**

For the residents of Birao, Am-Dafock, Tiringoulou, Boromata, and Ouanda-Djallé, this decision comes amid positive progress in peacebuilding, but also against the backdrop of the consequences of the conflict in Sudan and the violence that occurred in Am-Dafock in June 2026. The continuation of MINUSCA is seen as a strong signal in favor of continuing efforts toward peace, the protection of civilians, and support for national authorities.

Issouf Abdouramane, a community leader and member of the monitoring committee for the Am-Dafock local peace agreement, welcomed the decision, which meets the aspirations of local communities.

“We are pleased with the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate. The Mission has provided us with significant support in our efforts to negotiate and promote peace. From Birao to Am-Dafock, including Ouanda-Djallé, Matala, Dongore, Tiringoulou, and Boromata, MINUSCA works alongside communities and intervenes whenever there is a security issue to protect the people,” he said.

In his view, the people now expect these efforts to continue in order to bring about a lasting improvement in their living conditions.

“We want peace and the free movement of people and goods. We hope that this renewal will strengthen assistance to the people—particularly in Tissifongoro—in terms of access to drinking water, healthcare, and protection. We also hope for improved security in the Vakaga region so that everyone can go about their daily lives in peace,” he added.

Issouf Abdouramane also welcomed the recent deployment of the MINUSCA Force to Tiringoulou, which began on October 26, 2026, to help protect civilians in that area.

Oumar Idriss, a community leader in Toumou, also believes that the renewal of the mandate constitutes recognition of the joint efforts of the Central African Government and MINUSCA in support of peace and security.

“I am pleased with the efforts made to ensure that MINUSCA’s mandate was renewed. We saw its actions in Am-Dafock following the attack on June 30, 2026, including support for the deployment of the FACA, the protection of civilians, and the facilitation of humanitarian aid delivery. In Tiringoulou, Sikikede, and Boromata as well, MINUSCA supported national authorities in strengthening the state’s presence and better protecting the population,” he emphasized.

In his view, the Mission has played a major role in consolidating peace in the prefecture. “MINUSCA has contributed enormously to stability and social cohesion in Vakaga. Its continued presence is good news for the communities,” he asserted.

Guisma Younouss, a member of the Organization of Central African Women (OFCA), emphasized that the renewal of the mandate represents an opportunity to further strengthen the promotion and protection of women’s rights. “We would like to see more training and awareness-raising activities on women’s rights in order to promote their participation in development and peacebuilding,” she said.

The prefecture’s administrative authorities also welcomed this decision. For the prefect of Vakaga, Judes Ngayoko, the renewal of the mandate confirms the importance of the partnership between the Central African Government, MINUSCA, and humanitarian actors in the search for sustainable solutions to the region’s challenges.

“I welcome the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate. Together with MINUSCA and other humanitarian actors, we have accomplished a great deal, especially following the crisis of June 30, 2026, which affected Am-Dafock. MINUSCA has supported the government in protecting civilians, deploying the Central African Armed Forces (FACA), and delivering humanitarian aid. However, security and humanitarian challenges persist in Am-Dafock, Boromata, and Sikikede—areas bordering Sudan and Chad. We must continue our efforts with MINUSCA in these various localities,” he stated.

In Am-Dafock, one of the areas hardest hit by the violence in June 2026, local authorities also expressed their relief. The subprefect of Am-Dafock, Abdel Kader Ramadan, believes that the Mission’s presence remains essential for the protection of the people living in this particularly vulnerable border area.

“The people of Am-Dafock and I welcome the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate. Without MINUSCA’s intervention, the worst would have happened in Am-Dafock during the attacks of June 30, 2026. We thank MINUSCA for taking in the people at its base to protect them. But security and humanitarian challenges remain because we are in an area with porous borders with Sudan. We hope that the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate will allow the Mission to redouble its efforts in Am-Dafock to better protect the people and consolidate peace,” he said.

For the head of the MINUSCA office in Birao, Amadou Moctar Diallo, this mandate renewal offers a new opportunity to preserve and consolidate the gains made in Vakaga. He added that this renewal also provides an opportunity to strengthen joint efforts with local and national actors to ensure better protection of civilians and lasting peace.

fields.title: République Démocratique du Congo : Présence operationnelle des partenaires de la reponse à l’epidemie d’Ebola au 31 Octobre 2026 - Les partenaires qui ont renseigné l outil 3W (Qui Fait Quoi Où ?) et appuient le plan SGI du Ministère de la Santé
fields.body:
Au 31 octobre 2026, le Cluster Santé en République démocratique du Congo recensait 95 acteurs humanitaires appuyant le plan du Système de gestion des incidents (SGI) du Ministère de la Santé pour la réponse à Ebola. Cette mobilisation rassemble 44 ONG internationales, 40 ONG nationales, 6 agences des Nations Unies, 3 agences intergouvernementales et 2 observateurs.

Les données collectées à travers l’outil 3W (« Qui fait Quoi, Où ? ») présentent la présence opérationnelle des partenaires et leurs contributions aux différents piliers de la riposte. Cette cartographie facilite la coordination, l’identification des complémentarités et la planification des interventions.

Les appuis couvrent la surveillance épidémiologique, la recherche active des cas et des contacts, les laboratoires, la prise en charge des patients ainsi que la prévention et le contrôle des infections. Ils comprennent également l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement, les points d’entrée, la logistique, la formation, le déploiement des ressources humaines et l’analyse des données.

Les partenaires contribuent aussi à la mobilisation communautaire, au soutien psychosocial, à la prise en charge alimentaire, à la protection et au maintien des services de santé essentiels.

Sous le leadership gouvernemental, ces contributions soutiennent une réponse coordonnée. Les informations présentées reflètent les déclarations des partenaires ayant renseigné l’outil 3W à cette date.
